title: The Reverse Mathematics of Analytic Measurability
summary: A classical theorem of Lusin states that all analytic sets are Lebesgue-measurable. In this article we established the reverse mathematical strength of Lusin's theorem, which depends on how precisely it is formalized. By doing so, we answer to a question of Simpson. Our main proof is motivated towards proving a specific version of that result, namely that analytic sets are Lesbesgue-regular, which requires the equality of the outer and inner measures of the set in question.
